missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine nominative agreement. 'Русский' takes the masculine ending to match 'город'. The relational adjective marks national origin rather than degree.
Strategic focus: Feminine nominative agreement. 'Русская' takes the feminine ending to match 'зима'. The collocation names a familiar national feature.
Strategic focus: Neuter nominative agreement. 'Русское' takes the neuter ending to match 'слово'. The everyday remark anchors the neuter form.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Русские' takes the plural ending to match 'песни'. The cultural image fixes the plural form.

missions.phrase: Мы изучаем русский язык в школе.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine accusative agreement. 'Русский' matches the inanimate masculine 'язык', whose accusative looks like the nominative. The classroom scene roots the form.
Strategic focus: Feminine accusative agreement. 'Русскую' takes the feminine accusative ending to match 'еду'. The kitchen scene shows the form in an oblique case.
Strategic focus: Feminine prepositional agreement. After 'в', 'русской' takes the feminine prepositional ending to match 'деревне'. The location phrase shows agreement in an oblique case.

missions.phrase: Он пишет статью о русском балете.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine prepositional agreement. After 'о', 'русском' takes the masculine prepositional ending to match 'балете'. The cultural topic anchors the oblique form.
Strategic focus: Plural instrumental agreement. After 'любуются', 'русскими' takes the plural instrumental ending to match 'дворцами'. The sentence extends agreement into the plural oblique case.
Strategic focus: Plural genitive agreement. After 'полон', 'русских' takes the plural genitive ending to match 'икон'. As a relational adjective, русский has no comparative form.
